title: Aging Phase Diagram and Exact Asymptotic Energies of Mixed Spherical Spin Glasses
authors: Johannes Lang, Vincenzo Citro, Luca Leuzzi, Federico Ricci-Tersenghi
abstract: We determine the aging phase diagram of mixed spherical $(p+s)$-spin glasses quenched from random configurations to zero temperature. Solving the asymptotic dynamical equations of Cugliandolo and Kurchan, we find transitions between aging states with one, two, and continuously many effective temperatures, including phases in which discrete and continuous hierarchies coexist. We obtain analytic expressions for the energies reached asymptotically by the dynamics. In models combining pairwise and higher-order interactions, and sufficiently separated interaction orders ($s>3$), a fully continuous phase exists, where the gradient descent relaxation converges to the algorithmic energy lower bound. Instead, in mixed models with only high-order interactions ($p\ge3$) the energy relaxation remains strictly above it. Numerical integration of the dynamical equations is consistent with the predicted two-step and mixed discrete--continuous aging states.
summary: This work theoretically maps the aging phase diagram for mixed spherical spin glasses quenched to zero temperature. By solving asymptotic dynamical equations, the authors classify various aging states based on the interaction mixture. The research provides exact expressions for the asymptotic energy, comparing it to the theoretical lower bound set by polynomial-time algorithms.
main_problem: The paper determines the aging phase diagram and calculates the exact asymptotic energies for mixed spherical spin glasses quenched to zero temperature.
main_result: The phase diagram exhibits complex transitions between aging states (e.g., 1-RSB, 2-RSB, FRSB) depending on the interaction mixture, and the asymptotic energy is compared against the algorithmic lower bound.
method: The analysis involves solving the asymptotic dynamical equations derived from Cugliandolo and Kurchan's theory, utilizing concepts from Replica Symmetry Breaking (RSB) hierarchy.
model_or_system: The system is a mixed spherical $(p+s)$-spin glass, characterized by a random Gaussian energy Hamiltonian combining pairwise ($p$) and higher-order ($s$) interactions.
key_observables: Asymptotic energy density ($E_\infty$), effective temperature ($X[C]$), and the classification of aging states (e.g., 1-RSB, FRSB).
important_parameters: Mixing weight ($\lambda$), interaction orders ($p, s$), and the quench temperature ($T=0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes ultrametricity and local equilibration at scale endpoints, and separates dynamics into stationary and aging components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-equilibrium phase diagrams for $(2+s)$ and $(3+s)$ models, showing transition lines, and also show numerical convergence of correlation functions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the asymptotic equations for the correlation and response functions, derives the energy density from stationary and aging contributions, and maps out the phase diagram based on solving these equations across different interaction mixtures.
why_interesting: The rigorous theoretical framework for characterizing non-equilibrium dynamics in complex energy landscapes, like those found in spin glasses, provides deep insights into relaxation processes relevant to many-body quantum systems.

The blue and red lines are the 1-RSB–1- FRSB and 1-FRSB–FRSB transitions given by Eqs. (10) and (12). In the FRSB phase, gradient flow reaches the algorith- mic bound Ealg.

Figure 2. Non-equilibrium phase diagram of the (3 + s) mod- els, plotted as 1 −λ versus s on logarithmic axes. Increas- ing λ (from top to bottom) yields the sequence 1-RSB, 2- RSB, 2-FRSB, 1-FRSB, and reentrant 1-RSB. The critical lines λ1-2 (orange), λ2-2F (green) and λ2F-1F (red) are deter- mined numerically, while λ1F-1 (blue) is given analytically by Eq. (A.26). All four lines meet at s = 10 and 1−λ = 1/21. For s < 10, the asymptotic solution is 1-RSB for every λ ∈[0, 1].

Figure 3. Asymptotic energies relative to the algorithmic bound Ealg. Top: physical energy E∞−Ealg (blue) and con- tinued marginal 1-RSB energy E1 −Ealg (red) for the (2 + 9) model. The dashed lines mark λ1-1F = 3/7 and λ1F-F ≃0.964. The 1-FRSB solution solves the paradox of having E1 < Ealg for λ ≳0.65. In the FRSB phase, E∞= Ealg. Bottom: energies of the 1-RSB (red), 1-FRSB (blue), 2-FRSB (green), and 2-RSB (orange) solutions of the (3 + 15) model, plotted against 1−λ. Each branch is shown over the domain in which the corresponding asymptotic solution exists. The physical energy is their upper envelope, which remains strictly above Ealg for any λ value.
